title: Impact of Income on Civil Conflict Using Rainfall Variation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS)

Why: Income (x) may be endogenous in the conflict equation due to omitted variables, reverse causality, or measurement error. Rainfall variation (z) is used as an instrument because it plausibly shifts agricultural income in developing regions but is arguably exogenous to conflict, conditional on controls.

Key assumptions:
- Relevance: Rainfall variation affects income (Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0). We will test via the first-stage F-statistic.
- Exclusion restriction: Rainfall affects conflict only through income, not directly or through other channels beyond included controls.
- Independence: Conditional on controls, rainfall is as good as randomly assigned with respect to unobserved determinants of conflict.
- Monotonicity (for LATE interpretation): An increase in rainfall does not decrease income for some units while increasing it for others.
- Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers across units via rainfall).

We estimate: y = β x + γ controls + ε, with x instrumented by z (and controls included in both stages).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load or install required packages
pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
to_install <- pkgs[!(pkgs %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s70_data.csv")

# Quick sanity check: instrument is binary {0,1} and variables are numeric
stopifnot(all(c("y","x","z","controls") %in% names(df)))
if(!all(df$z %in% c(0,1))) warning("z is not binary; proceeding but interpret accordingly.")

# 2) OLS (naive) for comparison
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_robust <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))

# 3) IV (2SLS) with controls
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = df)
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))

# Extract key IV coefficient and stats
iv_coef <- iv_robust["x","Estimate"]
iv_se   <- iv_robust["x","Std. Error"]
iv_t    <- iv_robust["x","t value"]
iv_p    <- iv_robust["x","Pr(>|t|)"]

# 4) First-stage relevance check (F-stat on excluded instrument z)
fs_full       <- lm(x ~ controls + z, data = df)
fs_restricted <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
fs_test <- anova(fs_restricted, fs_full)  # nested model F-test for z
fs_F   <- fs_test$F[2]
fs_p   <- fs_test$`Pr(>F)`[2]
fs_coef_z <- coef(fs_full)["z"]

# 5) Robust Durbin-Wu-Hausman (endogeneity) test via control-function approach
# First stage to get residuals
xhat <- fitted(fs_full)
vhat <- df$x - xhat
dwh_lm <- lm(y ~ x + controls + vhat, data = df)
dwh_ct <- coeftest(dwh_lm, vcov = vcovHC(dwh_lm, type = "HC1"))
dwh_p  <- dwh_ct["vhat","Pr(>|t|)"]

# 6) Robustness: IV without controls
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_noc_robust <- coeftest(iv_noc, vcov = vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC1"))
iv_noc_coef <- iv_noc_robust["x","Estimate"]
iv_noc_se   <- iv_noc_robust["x","Std. Error"]
iv_noc_p    <- iv_noc_robust["x","Pr(>|t|)"]

# 7) Print key numerical results clearly
cat("=== Main IV Result (2SLS with controls) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Beta_IV (effect of income on conflict): %.4f\n", iv_coef))
cat(sprintf("Robust SE: %.4f | t: %.2f | p-value: %.4g\n", iv_se, iv_t, iv_p))

cat("\n=== First-Stage Relevance ===\n")
cat(sprintf("First-stage coefficient of z on x (controlling for controls): %.4f\n", fs_coef_z))
cat(sprintf("Excluded instrument F-stat (z | controls): %.2f | p-value: %.4g\n", fs_F, fs_p))
cat("Rule of thumb: F > 10 indicates a strong instrument.\n")

cat("\n=== OLS (naive, for comparison) ===\n")
ols_coef <- ols_robust["x","Estimate"]; ols_se <- ols_robust["x","Std. Error"]; ols_p <- ols_robust["x","Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Beta_OLS: %.4f | Robust SE: %.4f | p-value: %.4g\n", ols_coef, ols_se, ols_p))

cat("\n=== Endogeneity (Robust Durbin-Wu-Hausman) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("p-value for residual (vhat) in outcome eq.: %.4g\n", dwh_p))
cat("Small p-value => x is endogenous; IV preferred over OLS.\n")

cat("\n=== Robustness Check: IV without controls ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Beta_IV (no controls): %.4f | Robust SE: %.4f | p-value: %.4g\n", iv_noc_coef, iv_noc_se, iv_noc_p))

# 8) Also report 95% robust CI for main IV estimate
alpha <- 0.05
crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df.residual(iv))
iv_ci_low  <- iv_coef - crit * iv_se
iv_ci_high <- iv_coef + crit * iv_se
cat("\n=== 95% Robust CI (main IV) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("[%.4f, %.4f]\n", iv_ci_low, iv_ci_high))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Higher income (driven by favorable rainfall) should reduce conflict incidence via higher opportunity costs of fighting and greater local resources for stability.
- Magnitude: With variables roughly standardized, a one-unit increase in income is expected to reduce conflict by about 0.2 to 0.6 units. In standardized terms, this corresponds to a moderate negative elasticity. The actual estimate will depend on instrument strength and control inclusion.
- First stage: Positive and statistically strong effect of rainfall on income (F-stat ideally > 10).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use rainfall variation as an instrument for income.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased income, driven by higher rainfall, reduces the likelihood of civil conflict.
